# Branch Mathematics / GURF

Canonical public technical reference. Publication synchronized 2026-11-25; recovered source developments through 2026-11-01.

- /branch-mathematics.html — frozen V1 / Edition 1.1 architecture; internally established in stated scope
- /gurf.html — response-specialized layer, with GRDE frozen at 008
- /updates.html — current publication, comparison, source trace, applications and reproducible downloads
- /seed-closure.html — November Seed provenance, adaptive observations, compact recovery, deterministic and set-valued closure
- /development.html — preserved 18–23 October proofs, exact certificates, executable files and implementation boundaries
- /audit.html — 645-entry October inventory plus 32 separately indexed November source-local summaries; 336 original entries concern BM
- /downloads/bm-2026-10-23/BM_Completeness_Public_2026-10-23.json — full public classification/evidence ledger
- /calculator.html — semicolon/newline symbolic input; advanced exact finite checks, finite predictor synthesis, real-rational quantum certificate verification, conditional decay budgets, and archived finite-lattice certificates
- /book.html — combined 13 November reading collection, dated Research Edition, additive notes and frozen V1
- /theorems.html — stable T01–T55, W01–W35 and FI01–FI42 registry
- /status.html — current gates and six broad BM research boundaries
- /steadman.html — frozen physical hypothesis and scoped additive lattice results
- /yang-mills.html — 24 finite-geometry certificates and the separate 11 October strong-coupling analytic bound

The 29 October 162-case comparison found agreement with established native methods, without establishing BM-specific practical advantage. The 13 November replay checks stored comparison outputs; it does not rerun CLUE. November Python tools are not browser calculator modes.

Classification labels: Defined; Theorem; Conditional theorem; Hypothesis; Physical interpretation; Missing equation. Evidence and lifecycle are separate. Counts do not measure truth, historical originality or percent completion.

The four-state continuous scalar Jordan squared-error interval is [(4+sqrt(13))/6, 1.2949] for unit coupling/horizon; the [1.2948,1.2949] interval is restricted to the stated cubic invariant family and fixed decoder. The unrestricted optimum remains open.

General finite algebraic quantum optimization is a proved quantifier-elimination procedure, not an implemented or executed general solver. The browser verifies the stated real-rational label-channel certificates. Uniform task-decay prediction requires the native decay/effectivity assumptions. Universal additive approximate infinite-horizon optimization is impossible in the stated computable-input class.

The analytic SU(2) lattice bound uses three spatial dimensions, the original Hamiltonian/link metric and |beta|<=3/64; the fixed-spacing limit uses strict inequality. This does not establish a four-dimensional continuum theory, weak-coupling continuum gap, universal physical RD current, new force, or a BM Navier–Stokes Clay solution. Internal proof records are not independent review or novelty certificates.
